---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Commands, roles and discoverable surfaces

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Inventory each command’s outcome, scope, availability and reversibility. Distinguish immediate commands from persistent selection before entering Buttons, Toggles, or the appropriate menu procedure.
2. Choose a discoverable primary surface plus contextual shortcuts. On Mac, consider the menu bar’s command catalog and keyboard access even when a toolbar or context menu also exposes the action.
3. Use consequence and current task to decide role/default, confirmation and recovery. Consult Alerts and Undo and redo when that decision depends on destructive behavior; preserve documented exceptions.
4. Deliver an action contract naming labels, roles, surfaces, shortcuts, availability and relevant pending/resolved behavior. Verify the action and its recovery rather than color alone.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make

name: apple-hig-home-screen-quick-actions
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting iOS and iPadOS app-icon shortcuts and their dynamic destinations.
---

# Make app-icon shortcuts land precisely

Read [the quick-action guide](../../references/home-screen-quick-actions.md). Treat the workflow as application advice; the documented component belongs to iOS/iPadOS.

Inspect high-value launch tasks, recent/context data, existing deep links, target platform, and create/review/adapt request. Identify whether actions are stable or dynamic and what happens if their referenced content disappears. Do not claim recent-item ordering or launch resolution is verified from labels alone.

Choose up to four useful shortcuts, preferably at least one when the app has a suitable task. Use concise outcome-oriented titles without app-name filler, adding a subtitle only to clarify. Prefer SF Symbols or template-derived monochrome glyphs rather than emoji. Update dynamic actions predictably from context and keep identity/destination consistent. Separate action dispatch from merely opening the app; a shortcut must resolve to its named task, including after a cold launch. These resolution details are application decisions to specify explicitly.

Implement the shortcut set/handlers, supply an action-to-destination specification, or review concrete wrong-target and stale-action defects. For Mac adaptation evaluate Dock menus; do not assert Home Screen quick actions exist on unsupported platforms.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a journal app offers six emoji-labelled actions including a deleted recent entry and `Open Journal App`. Decision: shortcuts should accelerate meaningful tasks, with reliable targets. After: keep `New Entry`, `Search Entries`, and valid recent entries within four actions; use meaningful monochrome icons and refresh stale references.

Deliver titles/subtitles/icons, update policy, and warm/cold destination behavior. Verify long localization, changed account, removed recent content, and interrupted launch resolution. Fail for exceeding the supported design limit, misleading destination, personal content from a former account, or a shortcut that only opens a generic home screen. Mark device Home Screen execution separately from handler inspection.

Load [launching](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-launching/SKILL.md) for launch continuity or [dock-menus](../apple-hig-dock-menus/SKILL.md) for Mac entry points.

# Home Screen quick actions Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/home-screen-quick-actions) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Holding an iOS/iPadOS app icon on Home Screen or Dock reveals app actions alongside system remove/edit-home commands. On devices with 3D Touch, pressing the icon with increased pressure also reveals these actions. Each action has a title, an icon whose side follows placement, and an optional subtitle. Text remains leading-aligned in left-to-right languages. Actions can update dynamically, such as recent conversations. ## Best practices Offer at least one useful high-value shortcut where possible and no more than four. Update predictably from context such as recent activity, location, time, or settings. Use concise outcome-oriented titles and optional clarifying subtitles without the app name or filler, allowing localization room. Use familiar SF Symbols or a glyph built from the official Quick Action template. Do not substitute emoji: quick-action symbols are monochrome and adapt for Dark Mode. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Quick actions are unsupported in macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Menus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/menus) #### Developer documentation — UIKit

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

name: apple-hig-launching
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting startup, launch screens, first usable content, restoration, and launch-to-task continuity.
---

# Make the first usable screen the launch outcome

Read [the launch guide](../../references/launching.md). This workflow is application advice; timing claims require measurement and launch screens apply only to specified platforms.

Inspect startup dependencies, first usable state, prior-state restoration, launch destinations, platform/orientation, and create/review/adapt mode. Distinguish launch from onboarding and initial downloads from readiness. Record measured time if available; do not call an unresponsive splash “launched.”

Remove unnecessary blocking work and provide useful interaction promptly. On iOS/iPadOS/tvOS match the static launch screen closely to first content/appearance/orientation to avoid flashes; omit unlocalized text and branding absent from the first screen. Place necessary branded splash/onboarding after launch rather than extending launch imagery. Restore meaningful prior detail, scroll, and window configuration. On TV use static rather than layered launch imagery. On visionOS consider an initial Shared Space window with explicit Full Space transition; Mac/watch/visionOS do not require the launch-screen component.

Implement the startup/restoration route, produce a dependency/first-screen/state specification, or review exact delay/mismatch defects. Preserve shortcut/deep-link intent so restoration cannot replace a newly requested target.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a recipe app shows a branded slogan until every photo downloads, then opens home instead of the previously read recipe. Decision: startup blocks useful content and loses continuity. After: match launch imagery to a usable initial structure, load nonessential photos progressively, and restore the recipe/scroll position unless a fresh external task overrides it.

Deliver the artifact, readiness definition, deferred work, launch-screen mapping, and restoration precedence. Verify cold/warm start, no network, rotation, appearance, prior state, and external launch target. Fail for false readiness, flash-inducing mismatch, lost task identity, or branded launch delay. Report measured versus estimated timing and actual native launch execution separately.

Load [loading](../apple-hig-loading/SKILL.md), [onboarding](../apple-hig-onboarding/SKILL.md), or [app-shortcuts](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-app-shortcuts/SKILL.md) for the next stage.

# Launching Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/launching) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Launch ends when the first usable screen is ready, including any initial download. Onboarding follows launch rather than replacing it. ## Best practices Aim for immediate interaction, generally within a few seconds. Provide a system launch screen on iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS; Mac, visionOS, and watchOS do not require one. Put any necessary branded splash in onboarding or after launch. Restore detailed previous state, including scroll position and window configuration, so reopening continues prior work. ## Launch screens The launch screen exists only to make startup appear fast. Match the first screen closely, including current orientation and appearance, to avoid flashes; if startup transitions from a plain color, use that color. Avoid text because this static content is not localized, and avoid advertising or an About-style presentation. Logos and other branding belong on the launch screen only when they are fixed elements of the first app screen. This section does not apply to macOS, visionOS, or watchOS. ## Platform considerations Launch screens apply to iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS; other platforms use their own launch behavior. ### iOS, iPadOS Launch in current orientation when supporting both portrait and landscape. For a single supported orientation, use it consistently and handle either direction of rotation into landscape correctly. ### tvOS Launch imagery is static rather than layered. Live-viewing apps can begin relevant live playback after a few seconds of inactivity where appropriate. ### visionOS Consider starting in Shared Space even for an immersive app. An initial window can supply context and loading time while letting the person explicitly choose the transition to Full Space alongside their other apps. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Onboarding](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) [Loading](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/loading) #### Developer documentation — Xcode — UIKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 10, 2024, June 21, 2023.

item.text: The brief identifies three problems: nine shortcuts dominated by settings, unlabeled icons, and “Track latest” opening the welcome screen while retaining stale package content. I’ll specify two stable task shortcuts and one conditional package shortcut, with explicit destinations for cold launch and removed packages.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > result.md <<'EOF'
# iPhone package tracker: revised Home Screen quick actions

## Scope and evidence

This is a framework-agnostic interaction specification based on "'`interface.md` and the installed apple-hig package. The supplied interface is a brief, not an executable implementation: it describes nine actions, mostly account settings, unlabeled icons, “Track latest” opening a generic welcome screen, and a stale package advertised when nothing is tracked. Individual settings labels, existing routes, account model, and package schema are not supplied.

The decisions below define proposed behavior. “Active package” means a tracked package that is neither delivered, archived, nor deleted; this is a product definition, not an Apple requirement. Equivalent existing domain states may be mapped explicitly during implementation.

## Decisions and action contract

Offer two stable shortcuts and a third only when a valid active package exists. Remove account settings from this surface; retain their ordinary in-app entry points. All actions are navigation or draft creation, never immediate data mutation. The same tasks must remain available inside the app.

Apple'"'s local [Home Screen quick actions guidance — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/home-screen-quick-actions#Best-practices) recommends useful, concise shortcuts, no more than four, predictable contextual updates, and familiar monochrome symbols rather than emoji. The exact two-plus-one set and ordering below are product decisions.

| Position / stable action ID | Visible title | Subtitle | Icon intent | Destination and availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 / "'`add-package` | Add Package | None | Monochrome plus glyph | Always offered. Open the tracking-number entry form, ready for input. Create no package until the user submits valid input. Cancel returns to the prior in-app context or package list on a cold start. |
| 2 / `view-packages` | View Packages | None | Monochrome shipping-box glyph | Always offered. Open the package list. With zero packages, show “No packages yet” and an Add Package action. |
| 3 / `track-latest` | Track Latest | None | Monochrome location glyph | Offer only with a validated active package. Open that exact package'"'s tracking detail, including status and last-update time. |

Every row has a text title as well as an icon. Use a familiar SF Symbol if available through the eventual platform integration, otherwise a monochrome glyph derived from the official Quick Action template. Exact assets and SDK identifiers remain implementation work. Let the system place icons and render the menu; do not encode left/right placement in custom artwork. No package names, addresses, or tracking numbers appear in shortcut text.

“Latest” means the active package with the most recent successful user tracking-detail visit, falling back to the most recently added active package. Break timestamp ties by stable package ID. Carrier background updates do not change this ranking. This is a deterministic product policy; it does not claim Apple prescribes recency ordering.

## Dynamic publication and destination identity

Publish a complete replacement set after local data is ready, after a successful tracking-detail visit, and after add, delivery, archive, deletion, or account changes. Keep the two stable actions in their positions. If there is no eligible package, publish only those two; do not publish a disabled or stale Track Latest row.

Bind Track Latest to an opaque package ID and its account/context generation at publication.
